ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, A is a schematic diagram of a long-distance power transmission line, and B is an image of the generator output voltage changing with time. When the total resistance of the user's electrical appliances increases, how does the power lost on the transmission line change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When the total resistance of the user's electrical appliances increases, the power lost on the transmission line decreases
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, A is a schematic diagram of long-distance power transmission; the left side is labeled “generator,” after which it is connected to a “step-up transformer,” then connected through two lines labeled “transmission line” to the “step-down transformer” on the right side, and finally supplies the “user.” In the figure, B is an image of the generator output voltage changing with time; the vertical axis is labeled u/V, the horizontal axis is labeled t/s, the voltage shows an alternating-current sinusoidal change, the peak value is about ±500 V, and the period is about 0.02 s. Then reason: when the generator output voltage and the transformer turns ratio remain unchanged, the total resistance of the user's electrical appliances increases, which is equivalent to the load resistance becoming larger, so the current on the user side decreases; from the transformer current relationship, it can be known that the current in the transmission line also decreases accordingly. The transmission line resistance R_line remains unchanged, and the power lost on the transmission line satisfies P_loss = I_line^2 R_line, so when the transmission line current decreases, the lost power decreases.
